title: Key Concepts of Prosocial Behaviour
author: 6a2744013899d0fc4c7f52dc
chapter_outcomes: Prosocial behaviour, positive action that benefits others, including: development of prosocial behaviour with age, examples of prosocial behaviour, including helping, sharing, and caring
Individual factors: unique features of a person which can affect prosocial behaviour, examples include personality, age, biological factors
Situational factors: factors external to a person which can affect prosocial behaviour, examples include location, proximity, environmental factors
Neurotransmitters, chemical signals produced by a nerve cell and released to the target cell
The function of the neurotransmitter serotonin in prosocial behaviour
The function of the hormone oxytocin in prosocial behaviour

The role of the following brain areas in prosocial behaviour: prefrontal cortex (part of the cerebral cortex involved in attention, emotional expression and social behaviours), amygdala (active in empathetic responses)
Heritability, a measure of the extent to which differences in a characteristic or behaviour can be explained by differences in genes
Heritability of prosocial behaviour, including the similarities of monozygotic (MZ) and dizygotic (DZ) twins
Argument for the biological explanation of prosocial behaviour: support from the named study: heritability of social responsibility (Rushton)

Argument against the biological explanation of prosocial behaviour: heritability is not entirely responsible for prosocial behaviour, there are also environmental influences, for example, social groups and roles
Application of knowledge of the biological explanation of prosocial behaviour to novel scenarios
Social identity, part of a person's identity that that comes from belonging to social groups, such as family and ethnicity

Tajfel and Turner's social identity theory: stages including social categorisation, social identification, and social comparison, relationship between group membership and self-esteem, dynamics of ingroups (groups that a person is a member of), outgroups (groups that a person is not a member of)
Tajfel and Turner's social identity theory in understanding prosocial behaviour: role of shared identity in prosocial behaviour, helping and ingroup favouritism
Argument for the social identity theory of prosocial behaviour: support from the named study: helping behaviour (Levine et al., study 1 only)

Argument against the social identity theory of prosocial behaviour: prosocial behaviour is not just influenced by social identity. For example, individual differences between members of the same social groups and cultural factors
Application of knowledge of the social identity theory of prosocial behaviour to novel scenarios

Bandura's social learning theory: four processes of social learning: attention, retention, reproduction, and motivation; types of models: live, symbolic, verbal instruction; the role of vicarious reinforcement

Bandura's social learning theory in understanding prosocial behaviour: observation of prosocial behaviours, imitation of models' prosocial behaviour, vicarious reinforcement, as motivation for prosocial behaviour (frequency of a behaviour increases after observing others (models) being rewarded for the same behaviour)

Bandura's social learning theory in understanding prosocial media use: modelling (learning by imitating or copying others (models)), parental mediation of media use (strategies parents use to check, control and discuss children's media use), empathy (ability to understand another's feelings and see things from their point of view)
Argument for Bandura's social learning theory of prosocial behaviour: support from the named study: prosocial media (Prot et al., study 1 only)

Argument against Bandura's social learning theory of prosocial behaviour: environmental influences are not entirely responsible for prosocial behaviour, there are also biological factors, for example, hormones, neurotransmitters, brain areas and genetics
Application of knowledge of Bandura's social learning theory to novel scenarios
